title: Relay Shift Scrapbook: Ops Weeknote — Oct 11 2027
content:
Purpose: quick, messy weekly scrapbook for the relay shift crew. Use this as the canonical short-form notes for the week (incidents, SLO blips, oddball traces, and on-call relay details). Not a formal postmortem — that's tracked in ENGSRE-4281.

Attendees / relays: Maya (today -> primary), Ethan (shadow), Sofia (next shift), Leo (backup for infra), Aisha (observability consult on call).

TL;DR:
- Single customer-facing degradation on 2027-10-09 22:14 UTC — elevated 99th p99 latency for text generation routes for ~38 minutes.
- Root cause: transient GPU pod storm during autoscale event + delayed cache warmup for KV prefixes.
- SLO impact: hosted-api/produce-text p99 slipped from 220ms -> 1.8s during window; error rate unchanged. Current weekly SLO burn: 0.72% (target 99.5 availability).
- Hot actions: tweak autoscaler cooldown, add warmup prefetch to prefix cache path, create a small canary for new batch size.

Incident notes (chronological):
1) 2027-10-09 22:10 — Alert: latency_p99_hosted_text > 800ms (pager). On-call receives, paged to oncall primary.
2) 22:12 — Bridge created (bridge-id: relay-20271009-1). Quick triage: CPU stable, GPUs healthy, but spike in Pod restarts for model-pool-3b-v2 (3 restarts).
3) 22:18 — Observability shows a flood of cold starts where KV cache misses coincided with high concurrent prefix lengths (large customer sessions).
4) 22:25 — Brief rollout check: a config change to autoscaler memory threshold was pushed 2h prior (PR 7892). Rollback isn't required but flagged as contributing.
5) 22:40 — Mitigation: pinned a subset of traffic to model-pool-3b-v1 (lower sequence length profile) and temporarily increased pod warmup concurrency. Latency returns to baseline by 22:48.

Notes I scribbled in the bridge: "Weird pattern: restarts clustered on single AZ (us-west2-b) — schedule fault domain check. Cache misses amplified because new long-session feature sent long prompt prefixes. Need to instrument prefix-length histogram per route."

SLO / metrics snapshot:
- Service: hosted-api/produce-text
- Weekly p99: 0.228s baseline -> spike to 1.8s during incident
- Error rate (5m window): steady at 0.03%
- SLO burn this week: 0.72% (projected at 0.9% if similar event repeats)
- Observability gaps: don't currently threshold on prefix-length distribution. Add a signal.

Runbook & playbook observations:
- Relay playbook step 3 (queue pressure check) unclear when model pools use mixed quantized variants. Add a clarifying note.
- Runbook currently suggests rollback for autoscaler changes — we didn't roll back; we mitigated via traffic pinning and warmup as a valid step. Update runbook to include traffic pinning and warmup as a valid step.

Action items (owner -> eta):
- Ethan: add per-route prefix-length telemetry + dashboard (KPI) — ETA 2027-10-18.
- Sofia: add a playbook step for "traffic pinning" and sign-off with product (doc PR) — ETA 2027-10-15.
- Leo: investigate AZ-aligned pod restarts; check node-level kubelet logs and schedule maintenance window with infra if needed — ETA 2027-10-14.
- Maya: follow up on PR 7892 (autoscaler threshold tweak) with release-engineering and coordinate a small canary for the change — ETA 2027-10-13.
- Aisha: prototype a KV-prefix prefetcher (prototype notes in /confluence) and estimate CPU/memory tradeoffs — ETA 2027-10-25.

Follow-ups and open questions: 
- Did PR 7892's threshold change significantly increase scale-down aggressiveness? Need a synthesis from release-engineering.
- How common are long-prefix sessions across top 10 tenants? Product to provide sample distribution.
- Consider a short-term mitigator: enforce a max-prefix-length per tenant or background warmup on accepted sessions. Are there product constraints?

Meeting minutes — weekly ops touch (2027-10-11 09:30 PDT):
- Quick recap of incident, owners confirmed for action items.
- Decision: do NOT rollback PR 7892 immediately; instead, deploy traffic pin + telemetry.
- Decided to add prefix-length histogram to SLO dashboard and create an alert when 95th prefix length > 4k tokens for a route.
- Agreed to a 2-week canary for autoscaler tweak with traffic shaping by tenant.

Handoff sketch for next shift (Sofia):
- Priority #1: unblock telemetry — confirm Ethan's dashboard surfaces by start of shift. If not, escalate to Aisha to add a temporary metric.
- Priority #2: validate Leo's node findings; if a node-type regression is found, escalate to infra slack (#infra-ops).
- Priority #3: roll canary plan meeting (Thu 10/14 10:00 PT) — invite product, release-eng, SRE, and one customer success rep for visibility.

Retro / what worked:
- Quick traffic pinning prevented a longer outage. The playbook team's idea to route by sequence-profile saved us time.
- Observability team responded fast with correlated traces; the new trace-sampling tweak made memory of cold starts visible.

Retro / what needs work:
- Insufficient pre-rollback decision matrix in the runbook. We need clearer guidance for config changes with autoscaler effects.
- No existing alert for prefix-length distribution — we had to derive it manually.
- Zone skew of restarts needs deeper triage.

Random notes / to self:
- Slack thread: #sre-bridge contains quick raw bridge log (search "relay-20271009-1").
- Consider adding a smoke canary that exercises KV cache warmup path every deploy. Could run as a periodic job.
- Draft micro-postmortem to be formalized in ENGSRE-4281; this doc remains an ops-weeknote snapshot.

Appendix (useful links):
- Incident ticket: ENGSRE-4281
- Bridge chat: slack://thread?team=T12345&id=Grelay20271009
- PR referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892
- Runbook page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/12345/relay-shift-playbook

End of note.

[notes-to-self]: leave this doc as ephemeral weekly cookbook; move finalized action items and formal postmortem outcomes to ENGSRE-4281 and runbook PRs.
